questions.text: How could rim continuity, floor morphology and internal structures be investigated for {crater}? Propose distinct, executable analytical approaches, explain the evidence each requires, and state what the available data can support.
answer_requirements: For each approach, specify its objective, steps, evidence files and limitations; avoid counting paraphrases as additional approaches.
Distinguish visible morphology, features requiring measurement and explanations of their origin.
Treat catalogue morphology codes as historical records rather than ground truth.

questions.text: How could east-west topographic asymmetry in {crater} be tested while distinguishing internal relief from regional background slope? Propose an analysis workflow and necessary checks, without treating the maximum-to-minimum elevation difference along the existing central profile as crater depth.
answer_requirements: When using topographic evidence, identify the elevation reference, units and profile location.
Explain how centre offsets, sampling direction and regional slope could affect the conclusions.
If topography is not selected, acknowledge that elevation asymmetry cannot be tested and identify the missing evidence.

questions.text: How could the spatial correspondence between rims or internal structures in images of {crater} and elevation changes be tested? Propose joint analyses and explain how discrepancies could be attributed to registration problems, resolution differences or possible geomorphic differences.
answer_requirements: Explain explicitly how the two types of evidence are related, rather than merely listing modalities.
Acknowledge that a shared target-centred projection does not establish precise registration of the source products.
If imagery or topography is missing, state which parts cannot be completed and avoid claiming that correspondence has been confirmed.

questions.text: Which testable hypotheses of subsequent modification could be proposed from the local morphology and regional context of {crater}? For each hypothesis, specify supporting and counterevidence to seek, alternative explanations, and distinctions that the current data cannot resolve.
answer_requirements: Distinguish observations from working hypotheses without presupposing a particular modification process.
Allow an assessment of insufficient evidence when support is lacking; multiple mechanisms are not mandatory.
Do not infer composition, absolute age, confirmed volcanic activity or impact parameters from grayscale imagery alone.

questions.text: For the impact structure {crater}, which combinations of impactor size, speed, incidence angle and target thermal state could produce a final diameter similar to the observations? Design a procedure for screening equivalent parameter families and explain how crater-shape or internal-structure observations could exclude some combinations. Provide no numerical parameter ranges without an applicable simulation grid.
answer_requirements: Distinguish final diameter from transient crater diameter and define the incidence-angle convention, units and applicable model scale.
Specify diameter measurement error and matching tolerance before comparing parameter combinations; explain retention, rejection and indeterminate cases.
Check scale and target-condition applicability before transferring parameters or scaling relations from the Caloris basin to this target.
When traceable simulation outputs are unavailable, describe the proposed tests and missing evidence without fabricating parameter grids, confidence intervals or exclusions.
quantitative_prerequisites: A versioned real simulation grid covering the target scale, impact parameters and target conditions
Consistent crater-shape definitions, scales and error models for simulations and observations

questions.text: If several impact models match the observed diameter of {crater}, which additional observation among floor relief, rim geometry and internal structure is most promising for distinguishing them? Design comparisons that add observations individually and explain why overlapping predictions or large observational errors may prevent exclusion of a model.
answer_requirements: Compare the acceptable model set under the diameter constraint alone with sets obtained by adding individual observations.
Distinguish actual discriminatory power from manually assigned selector capability scores; those scores do not measure information gain.
Account for spatial registration, resolution and shared data origins, avoiding independent double-counting of correlated errors.
Without model predictions and measurement errors, do not claim to have calculated information gain or excluded models.
quantitative_prerequisites: Candidate simulations satisfying the diameter constraint and their predictions for additional observations
Reproducible measurements and uncertainties for the target rim, floor and internal structures
Prespecified model-acceptance criteria and treatment of correlated errors

questions.text: If reliable measurements show that {crater} is shallower than reference craters of comparable size, how could later infilling and topographic relaxation be distinguished from regional background slope or measurement bias? Propose predictions that could be supported or refuted, identify existing observations and additional evidence that could distinguish the explanations, and first verify whether the target is actually shallower.
answer_requirements: Test the premise first; the maximum-to-minimum difference along a central profile is not a crater-depth measurement.
Justify reference-crater comparability in diameter, geological setting and data quality.
For each explanation, identify expected morphological or topographic features, counterexamples and cases that remain ambiguous.
Without applicable forward models or other independent constraints, do not infer fill thickness, relaxation time or absolute age.
quantitative_prerequisites: Reviewed rim and floor measurements with regional-background correction
Comparable reference-crater data and selection criteria
Applicable infilling or relaxation forward models, parameter ranges and literature support
